name: Cepheus Flare
source_reference: Zucker, C., Speagle, J. S., Schlafly, E. F., et al. 2019, ApJ, 879, 125, 'A Large Catalog of Accurate Distances to Local Molecular Clouds: The Gaia DR2 Edition' (arXiv:1902.01425) - 'Cepheus Near' cloud component: 352 pc +/- 1 pc (statistical) +/- 18 pc (systematic); error_pc here is the quadrature sum of the two quoted terms.
source_catalog: Zucker et al. 2019 (Gaia DR2 3D dust-based molecular cloud distances)
notes: Position (ra/dec) taken from the SIMBAD entry 'NAME Cepheus Flare' (otype MoC), the closest single-point designation SIMBAD offers for the complex; SIMBAD carries no parallax/distance for this extended entry, so distance is taken from Zucker et al. 2019 instead (spec S10: prefer Gaia-era literature to a stale/missing SIMBAD distance). The Cepheus Flare is in reality several individually Gaia-resolved dark clouds (L1148, L1158, L1177, L1217, L1219, L1235, L1251, L1228) spanning 330-368 pc (Dzib et al. 2021, MNRAS, 505, 5164, 'The Gaia view of the Cepheus flare', arXiv:2105.10039); the complex also spans ~90x60 pc in the plane of the sky per that paper (visual.size_pc uses the larger axis). This record collapses that structure to one MVP centroid using the Zucker et al. 2019 'Cepheus Near' value, which falls within the Dzib range.

name: Cepheus OB2
source_reference: Szilagyi, M., Kun, M., Abraham, P. & Marton, G. (2023), "The Gaia view of the Cepheus OB2 association", MNRAS, 520(1), 1390-1410 (arXiv:2301.02346). Gaia DR3 clustering resolves the association into 13 subgroups spanning heliocentric distances of 829-944 pc along the line of sight, centred at Galactic (l,b) = (102.1 deg, +4.6 deg); the classical literature value (Contreras et al. 2002, ApJ, 572, 926) is ~900 pc. distance_pc/error_pc here are the midpoint/half-range of the quoted Gaia DR3 829-944 pc subgroup spread, not a formal single-value parallax uncertainty - no single-number mean distance + error is given in the source for the association as a whole.
notes: Position is the SIMBAD 'Ass Cep OB 2' centroid (ra=327.75, dec=60.0 deg), independently verified to correspond to Galactic (l,b) = (102.11, 4.64) deg, matching Szilagyi et al. (2023)'s quoted central coordinates for the association.

name: Cepheus OB3
source_reference: Nagy, Zs., Abraham, P., Kospal, A. et al. (2022), "Photometric and spectroscopic study of the burst-like brightening of two Gaia-alerted young stellar objects", MNRAS, 516, 2. Distance to Cep OB3 of 816 +/- 53 pc obtained from a Gaussian fit to Gaia EDR3 parallax-based distances (Bailer-Jones et al. 2021) of 235 quality-filtered (RUWE < 1.4, parallax significant > 5 sigma) association members drawn from Jordi et al. (1996) and Getman et al. (2009).
notes: Position is the SIMBAD 'NAME III CEP ASSOC' centroid.

name: Cepheus OB4
source_reference: Wiesneth, B., Muzic, K. & Almendros-Abad, V. (2025), "Internal dynamics and structure of Cepheus OB4: The asymmetric expansion of Berkeley 59", A&A, 703, A193 (arXiv:2509.19175). Gaia DR3 astrometry gives a distance of 1009 +/- 12 pc to Berkeley 59, the dominant central massive-star cluster of the Cep OB4 association / H II bubble.
notes: Position and distance are for Berkeley 59 (SIMBAD 'Cl Berkeley 59'), the dominant central cluster of Cep OB4 - its SIMBAD position (ra=0.57, dec=67.441) matches the wider association's own SIMBAD centroid ('Ass Cep OB 4', ra=0.50, dec=67.70) to within 0.3 deg. Earlier literature (Kun, Kiss & Balog 2008, Handbook of Star Forming Regions Vol. I, arXiv:0809.4761) placed the Cep OB2/OB3/OB4 group collectively at a coarser 600-900 pc range; the Gaia DR3 Berkeley 59 value is adopted here as the more precise, modern figure.

notes: Position (ra/dec) is the SIMBAD centroid for 'Cl Melotte 25'. Independently cross-checked against the SIMBAD parallax on file for the same object (plx_value=21.052 mas -> ~47.5 pc), which agrees closely. Consistent with the ~47.0 pc value used for this object in Story #57.

name: Local Bubble
source_reference: Alves, M.I.R., Boulanger, F., Ferriere, K. & Montier, L. (2018), "The Local Bubble: a magnetic veil to our Galaxy", A&A, 611, L5 (doi:10.1051/0004-6361/201832637). Center position reused from Story #62's models/local_bubble.yaml ellipsoid-model center_pc = (x=10.2, y=33.6, z=0.0) pc, itself Alves et al. (2018) Table 1's fitted off-centred-spheroid offset (Sun at 0.58 of the semi-minor axis from the ellipsoid centre, along l=73 deg, b~0 deg) scaled by the paper's approximate a_pc=60 pc physical anchor (Sec. 1, citing Puspitarini et al. 2014, A&A, 566, A13).
notes: This is a single-point/centroid catalog-object representation of the Local Bubble (spec Idea.md §9 seed list, §15 MVP 'center + approximate radius' allowance), distinct from the separate, more detailed ellipsoid geometry in Story #62's models/local_bubble.yaml (which this entry deliberately does not duplicate or modify). No formal uncertainty is available for the centroid position itself in the source (Alves et al. 2018 fit shape/orientation, not an absolute distance, with error bars only on the dimensionless shape parameters - see models/local_bubble.yaml for those); the 60 pc anchor behind this position, and visual.size_pc here (approximating the semi-minor axis as a representative radius), are both order-of-magnitude, not precision-fit, figures. Position/distance were reverse-derived from center_pc via astropy Galactic->ICRS and round-trip verified to reproduce x=10.2, y=33.6, z=0.0 pc through this project's own coordinates.derive_galactic_coordinates().

name: Orion OB1
source_reference: Kounkel, M., Hartmann, L., Loinard, L., et al. 2018, AJ, 156, 84, 'The APOGEE-2 Survey of the Orion Star-forming Complex. II. Six-dimensional Structure' (arXiv:1805.04649) - kinematic group 'Orion D' (the population tracing the classical OB1a/OB1b belt stars, extending toward Rigel): 350 +/- 3 pc from APOGEE-2 + Gaia DR2 astrometry.
notes: SIMBAD's entry for this association is 'NAME Ori I' (otype As*; ra/dec taken from that entry) - Blaauw's original Roman-numeral naming for Orion's first-catalogued OB association, i.e. Orion OB1. Kounkel et al. 2018 find the classical OB1a/OB1b sky-area boundaries (Blaauw 1964: 199<l<210 deg, -21<b<-12 deg) do not cleanly map onto their kinematically distinct groups; their 'Orion D' group is the closest match to the OB1a/OB1b belt population and is used here as the representative distance. A separate, foreground-superimposed kinematic group 'Orion C' (the sigma Ori cluster, part of classical OB1b) sits at 406 +/- 4 pc in the same paper and is not separately represented in this MVP record.

name: Perseus OB2
source_reference: Ortiz-Leon, G. N., Loinard, L., Dzib, S. A., et al. 2018, ApJ, 865, 73, 'The Gould's Belt Distances Survey (GOBELINS). V. Distances and Kinematics of the Perseus Molecular Cloud' - combined VLBA + Gaia DR2 trigonometric parallax distance to IC 348, the principal embedded cluster of the Perseus OB2 association: 321 +/- 10 pc.
notes: Position (ra/dec) taken from the SIMBAD entry 'Ass Per OB 2' (otype As*), the association-level SIMBAD record; that entry's own parallax field (plx_value=2.67266 mas -> ~374 pc, a single-star measurement) was deliberately NOT used, per spec S10 guidance to prefer a dedicated Gaia-era literature distance over a thin/stale SIMBAD field. Distance instead uses IC 348, the association's principal cluster, as representative. A second major sub-cluster, NGC 1333, is separately measured at 293 +/- 22 pc in the same paper and is not separately represented in this MVP record.

name: Pipe Nebula
source_reference: Dzib, S. A., Loinard, L., Ortiz-Leon, G. N., et al. 2018, ApJ, 868, 32, 'Distances and Kinematics of Gould Belt Star-forming Regions with Gaia DR2 Results' (arXiv:1810.01917) - Barnard 59 (B59), the only actively star-forming core in the Pipe Nebula: mean trigonometric parallax of 6.12 +/- 0.19 mas from ~20 Gaia DR2 YSOs corresponds to 163 +/- 5 pc.

name: Scorpius-Centaurus Association
source_reference: de Zeeuw, P. T., Hoogerwerf, R., de Bruijne, J. H. J., Brown, A. G. A., Blaauw, A. 1999, AJ, 117, 354, 'A HIPPARCOS Census of the Nearby OB Associations' - mean subgroup distances: Upper Scorpius (US) 145 pc, Upper Centaurus-Lupus (UCL) 140 pc, Lower Centaurus-Crux (LCC) 118 pc. Still the standard subgroup-distance reference used by Gaia-era Sco-Cen studies (e.g. Damiani, F., et al. 2019, A&A, 623, A112, arXiv:1807.11884, which restricts its Gaia DR2 census to <200 pc and finds ~90% of known massive members within 100-170 pc, consistent with these subgroup values rather than superseding them with one number).
source_catalog: Hipparcos (de Zeeuw et al. 1999); consistent with Gaia DR2 (Damiani et al. 2019)
notes: Sco-Cen is the nearest OB association to the Sun but comprises 3 kinematically/spatially distinct subgroups (Upper Sco, Upper Cen-Lup, Lower Cen-Crux) spanning tens of pc in depth - the current schema has no sub-group representation, so this is deliberately simplified to a single MVP centroid, per issue #59 guidance. distance_pc is the unweighted mean of the 3 published subgroup distances (134.3 pc); distance.error_pc is the population standard deviation across those 3 subgroups (11.7 pc) - this is a depth-spread proxy, NOT a formal parallax/fit uncertainty, and should not be conflated with one. Position (ra/dec) is taken from the SIMBAD entry 'NAME Upper Sco-Cen' (otype As*), the closest single-point designation SIMBAD offers for the complex as a whole. A future story could add the 3 subgroups as separate records with `group.primary` set to this association's id.

name: Vela Supernova Remnant
source_reference: Dodson, R., Legge, D., Reynolds, J.E. & McCulloch, P.M. (2003), "The Vela Pulsar's Proper Motion and Parallax Derived from VLBI Observations", ApJ, 596, 1137 (arXiv:astro-ph/0302374). VLBI parallax of the embedded pulsar PSR B0833-45 = 3.4 +/- 0.2 mas, equivalent to a distance of 293 (+19/-17) pc; adopted here as the remnant's distance per standard convention that the Vela SNR shares the distance of its associated pulsar.
notes: Coordinates are those of the embedded pulsar PSR B0833-45 (SIMBAD 'NAME Vela Pulsar'), ~0.4 deg from the SIMBAD-catalogued extended-remnant centroid ('NAME Vela', SNR G263.9-03.3; ra=128.5, dec=-45.833) - within the remnant's ~4 deg angular radius and negligible (~2 pc) at this distance. error_pc uses the larger (+19 pc) of the source's asymmetric +19/-17 pc uncertainty, since this schema's error_pc is a single symmetric value. visual.size_pc ~= 40 pc is an approximate physical diameter derived from the remnant's commonly quoted ~8 deg angular diameter (ROSAT X-ray survey era literature, e.g. Aschenbach 1998 and successors) at the adopted VLBI distance - an order-of-magnitude figure, not a formally fitted size.
